card.text: Explore Earth in 3D with cssEarth. Orbit our home planet, discover its surface and atmosphere, and browse scientific facts in your browser.

introduction.text: Earth (our home planet) is the third planet from the Sun, and the fifth largest planet. It’s the only place we know of inhabited by living things.

normal.title: Blue Marble Next Generation
normal.summary: NASA Blue Marble, July 2004. Cloud-free land and ocean mosaic with brighter display midtones.

clouds.title: Blue Marble cloud composite
clouds.summary: Archival NASA clouds over a brighter July 2004 surface mosaic. This is not live weather.

topography.title: GEBCO land and seafloor heights
topography.summary: GEBCO_2026 modeled terrain. Colors show height and depth relative to mean sea level; ocean depths include estimates.

night-lights.title: Black Marble annual night lights · 2025
night-lights.summary: 2025 annual snow-free satellite radiance. Warm false color; logarithmic scale. Gray: missing data or outside 75°N–65°S. Aurora can remain at high latitudes. NASA Black Marble / Jurij Stare, lightpollutionmap.info.

enso.title: ENSO: sea-surface temperature anomalies · 7 Sept 2026
enso.summary: NASA MUR · 1 km source imagery · 7 Sept 2026. Sea-surface temperature departure from the 2003–2014 average. NASA colors saturate below −3 and at +3 °C. Gray: land, ice, or unavailable imagery.

cross-section.title: Interior structure model
cross-section.summary: A cut through Earth’s crust, rocky mantle, liquid outer core and solid inner core. Layer sizes follow the NASA Science model; colors are schematic.

mantle-tomography.title: GLAD-M35 mantle tomography
mantle-tomography.summary: Red and blue map slower and faster mantle waves relative to the mean at each depth. This is not temperature. Crust and core colors are schematic; gray marks depths outside the model.
